answer: Permafrost is the honest ledger. On the tundra, nothing decays and nothing hides: every season a willow survives stays readable in the ground, while tall imported saplings freeze the first winter. Trust is not a score you declare - it is growth the frost itself can verify, small, slow, ring by ring. The rich coat comes later: sable is what the tundra pays those who actually overwintered, not those who stitched fur onto a portrait.
